review_notes: I read the whole file and its two downstream users, `Mathlib/Logic/Function/OfArity.lean` and `Mathlib/Data/Fin/Tuple/Curry.lean`. I checked the simp attributes on `const_zero` and `const_succ`. I also checked the `@[simps!]` equivalences and whether the type-level equations are simp lemmas. `const_zero` and `const_succ` look well oriented and terminating: `const_succ` peels one `n+1` per step and `vecTail_cons` then normalises the result. I found no loop and no competing rule. The only issue I'm reporting is the missing simp coverage for the type-level equations. I have not run Lean, so I don't know whether the suggested simp attributes would cause motive problems in existing proofs, such as in `Curry.lean`.

findings.excerpt:
theorem fromTypes_cons {n} (α : Type u) (p : Fin n → Type u) (τ : Type u) :
    FromTypes (vecCons α p) τ = (α → FromTypes p τ) := fromTypes_succ _ τ
findings.problem: The `const` lemmas in this file are `@[simp]`, but the type-level unfolding lemmas `fromTypes_nil` and `fromTypes_cons` are not. The comment on `fromTypes_succ` ('prefer `fromTypes_cons` when it (syntactically) applies') says these lemmas are meant to be the canonical way to reduce `FromTypes ![α, β] τ`. Yet `simp` can't normalise `FromTypes ![α, β] τ` to `α → β → τ`. The sibling API for the constant-family case, `OfArity`, tags `ofArity_zero` and `ofArity_succ` with `@[simp]`, so the two interfaces are inconsistent. The `fromTypes_succ` comment also gives no reason `fromTypes_succ` should stay non-simp. It would unfold `vecHead`/`vecTail` of an arbitrary `p`, so keeping it non-simp is the sensible choice. That makes it all the more notable that the cons and nil forms, which do give a clean normal form, are left without attributes.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `fromTypes_nil` and `fromTypes_cons` as `@[simp]`, keeping `fromTypes_succ` non-simp as the comment intends. `fromTypes_zero` could also be `@[simp]`, but it overlaps with `fromTypes_nil`. After `vecTail_cons` and `vecHead_cons` fire, the result is the canonical form `α → β → τ` for `![α, β]`. Check the uses in `Mathlib/Data/Fin/Tuple/Curry.lean` for motive problems before committing.
findings.benefit: Users and downstream proofs get `FromTypes ![α, β, …] τ` normalised to an ordinary arrow type by plain `simp`, as they already do for `OfArity`. The result is one canonical form, which also helps when `const` is simp-unfolded and the surrounding types would otherwise stay in `FromTypes` form.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem ofArity_succ (α β : Type u) (n : ℕ) :
    OfArity α β n.succ = (α → OfArity α β n) := fromTypes_succ _ _
